newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX JGB, Euroyen ease, Japan job, CPI as expected.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX JGB, Euroyen ease, Japan job, CPI as expected.

text.p: SIMEX Japanese government bonds (JGB) futures ended lower on Friday amid fears of reduced Bank of Japan's (BOJ) interest in bonds, dragging along with it the Euroyen futures, dealers said.

They said BOJ's scaled-back operations in the bond market earlier in the week prompted fears that the Ministry of Finance might curtail its bond purchases instead of buying them until April as generally expected.
"JGBs is still haunted by fears that the Ministry of Finance might cut back its buying," said a dealer with a European trading house.
"But volume is thin as today is seen as the final trading day before Monday's half day session," he said.
March JGBs futures settled at 124.48, down 37 ticks on a meagre volume of 280 lots.
Dealers pegged near-term support and resistance for March JGBs at 124.00 and 125.05.
Benchmark June Euroyen futures was flat at 99.406 in late trade. The forward contracts slipped several ticks on continued concerns over Japan's consumption tax hike in April.
"The further months were volatile. But this has been exaggerated by the thin volume," a dealer said.
He said market was unperturbed by Japan's announcement of its November consumer price index and unemployment data as they were within expectations and did not affect rate outlook.
Japan announced on Friday its November consumer prices index rose 0.5 percent year-on-year to 100.3. It also revealed November jobless rate fell to 3.3 percent from 3.4 percent in October.
Eurodollars were stable in light trade. March ended unchanged from its IMM close, at 94.46 on 4,315 lots.
